svg.aria-label: A continuous ink drawing for Lebanon. At the left, a cash box drawn open in three firm strokes, its lid tipped back, its inside empty — nothing marked within it. From high on the right, a single kiln-orange line — the only warm mark on the page — arcs the width of the sky and dives into the box's open mouth: money arriving from outside. From the box's foot a fine ink line runs out across the page and loops twice through itself — the same school day run twice — then rises gently toward the right edge and fades to dashes before reaching it: September, not yet paid for.
svg.title: The Still · Lebanon — an empty box, money arriving from outside, and a line that loops twice
svg.desc: At the left of the page stands an open cash box: two upright ink strokes and a floor between them, the lid a single stroke tipped back from the rim. Its interior is empty — the zero; nothing is drawn inside it. From the upper right corner a single kiln-orange line, the only warm thing on the page, crosses the whole sky in one long shallow arc and dives into the box's open mouth: the pooled fund, arriving from off the page to stand where a treasury should. From the box's lower right corner one fine ink line sets out across the page: it loops once through itself, runs on, loops a second time — the same buildings running the school year twice in a day — then rises gently and thins into short dashes that stop short of the right edge: the next September, declared but not yet paid for. No fills, no volumes; the line is the image; the ground is paper-cream.
